import pandas as pd

# File paths for source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_57/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_57/training_1.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # Columns: ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating']
source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # Columns: ['movie_id', 'title']

# Transformation plan:
# - The target table schema is ['title': string, 'size': integer, 'mean': float]
# - source0 has ratings per user per movie_id
# - source1 maps movie_id to title
# - We need to aggregate source0 by movie_id to get:
#     size = count of ratings per movie_id
#     mean = average rating per movie_id
# - Then join with source1 on movie_id to get the title
# - Finally, select columns ['title', 'size', 'mean'] as target schema

# Aggregate source0 by movie_id
agg_ratings = source0.groupby('movie_id').agg(
    size=('rating', 'count'),
    mean=('rating', 'mean')
).reset_index()

# Join aggregated ratings with source1 to get titles
merged = pd.merge(agg_ratings, source1, on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema
target_df = merged[['title', 'size', 'mean']]

# Ensure correct data types as per target schema
target_df['title'] = target_df['title'].astype(str)
target_df['size'] = target_df['size'].astype(int)
target_df['mean'] = target_df['mean'].astype(float)

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_57/target_multisource_cot.csv"
target_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_57/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_57/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source2_57_0 and Source2_57_1 on movie_id
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, how='inner', left_on='movie_id', right_on='movie_id')

# Group by title, aggregate count of rating as size and mean of rating as mean
result = joined.groupby('title', as_index=False).agg(
    size=('rating', 'count'),
    mean=('rating', 'mean')
)

# Write output with exact target schema and column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_57/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
